e.g. GO:0044255 - exactly what the obo source stores in identifier.  The filter is not cosmetic: OBO ontologies give oboinowl:id to OWL object and annotation properties as well as to classes, so a full GO extract yields 11 rows whose "identifier" is a relationship name - part_of, occurs_in, regulates, ends_during, happens_during, starts_during, has_part, positively_regulates, negatively_regulates, has_ontology_root_term, term_tracker_item. They loaded as GOTerms and sorted to the top of the class in the UI. column8: is_a parents (obo source fills OntologyTerm.parents).  The filter runs on the raw term, before the transform, and is not optional: in OWL, rdfs:subClassOf also points at anonymous class expressions (owl:Restriction, "part_of some X").  A full GO extract returns 92,208 superclass rows of which 16,178 are blank nodes and 3 are owl:Thing; without the filter iri_localname turned each blank node into a GOTerm whose identifier was its node id, adding 16k junk parents.  Restricting to the OBO namespace keeps legitimate cross-ontology parents (BFO, CARO), which still arrive as identifier-only stub items - filter harder if unwanted.
